root_cause.text: In `kernel/auditsc.c::__audit_log_capset()`, a copy-paste mistake assigned `new->cap_effective` to the CAPSET audit record’s `cap.inheritable` field, so audit logs reported the wrong inheritable capability set.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `context->capset.cap.inheritable = new->cap_effective;` to `context->capset.cap.inheritable = new->cap_inheritable;`, and the CVE description states CAPSET records “report cap_pi (process inheritable) with the value of cap_effective instead of cap_inheritable.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `context->capset.cap.inheritable = new->cap_effective;` to `context->capset.cap.inheritable = new->cap_inheritable;`, and the CVE description states CAPSET records “report cap_pi (process inheritable) with the value of cap_effective instead of cap_inheritable.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix audit capset logging to record the correct inheritable capabilities.
intent_record.what: In __audit_log_capset(), the value assigned to context->capset.cap.inheritable was changed from new->cap_effective to new->cap_inheritable.
intent_record.how: At runtime, audit records for capset operations will now log the process's actual inheritable capability set instead of incorrectly duplicating the effective set, making the recorded audit data accurate.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit e68b75a027bb94066576139ee33676264f867b87
Author: Eric Paris <eparis@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 11 21:48:22 2008 +1100

    When the capset syscall is used it is not possible for audit to record the
    actual capbilities being added/removed.  This patch adds a new record type
    which emits the target pid and the eff, inh, and perm cap sets.
    
    example output if you audit capset syscalls would be:
    
    type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1225743140.465:76): arch=c000003e syscall=126 succes
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full implementation of __audit_log_capset(). The vulnerable copy-paste mistake is present here: after storing the effective set with `ax->cap.effective = *eff;`, the code incorrectly assigns `ax->cap.inheritable = *eff;` instead of using the `inh` argument. This matches the root cause that the audit record reports the wrong inheritable capability set. There is no fix present in this function, since the correct handling would be `ax->cap.inheritable = *inh;` and that is not what the code does.
